caption:
Microsoft released the India cut of its Work Trend Index 2026 on 3 September. The headline number everyone is repeating: 32% of India's workforce now counts as "frontier professionals" — reported at roughly twice the global average.

Read past the number. Microsoft's own framing is that India's AI advantage is human. Forbes put it plainly in its analysis of the same report: productivity alone is not enough.

Which means output is no longer the scarce asset. Judgment is. And judgment is worthless if you don't have the standing to be believed when you offer it.

This is the gap most competent people sit in. The work is sound. The idea is right. It gets ignored until someone with more bearing says the same thing louder.

In command, you learn fast that an order delivered without authority is a suggestion. Bearing. Tone. Calculated silence. These are trainable. Start there.

topic.title: Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026: India's judgment advantage
topic.angle: Lumina's audience is competent but not credited, and this data externally proves the scarce asset is judgment and the standing to be believed — not more output.
topic.why_now: Microsoft released the India cut on 3 September 2026 and secondary analysis is still circulating, while the presence-and-authority angle (and the widely misreported 32% figure) remains unclaimed by the coaching niche.

rationale: A stark text-only card matches the plainspoken command tone and lets the single contrarian claim from the Microsoft data carry the post without decoration.
